Forecast draws from a fitted model

Source: R/model-spec.R
mt_forecast.Rd

Simulates future death rates on the grid. The result holds simulated paths (draws), so that uncertainty propagates correctly to derived quantities such as life expectancy.

Usage

mt_forecast(
  fit,
  h = 10,
  to = NULL,
  n_draws = 500,
  seed = NULL,
  predictive = FALSE,
  exposure = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

fit

An mt_fit object.

h

Forecast horizon in years.

to

Alternatively, the last year to forecast.

n_draws

Number of simulated paths.

seed

Random seed (NULL leaves the random number generator as is).

predictive

If TRUE, draws describe observable rates: for models of expected rates (such as lee_carter()), and for any model fitted to smoothed rates (step_smooth()), deaths are drawn given the rates of each draw and exposure and divided by the exposures. The deaths are Poisson, the observation model of the Poisson Lee-Carter model (Brouhns, Denuit and Vermunt 2002); for models with a negative binomial likelihood (stanmomo(family = "nb")) they are negative binomial with the model's dispersion. No other observation noise is added. Models of observed rates (rwd(), arima_series(), ets_series()) add nothing. Cells can have zero deaths (rate 0). Used by mt_backtest(), which sums the deaths to the observed cells before taking logarithms. If predictive intervals are too narrow on real data, that is a property of the model: see recalibrated(), ensemble() or overdispersed models such as stanmomo(family = "nb").

exposure

Exposures for predictive draws: array [age, period, stratum] or matrix [age, stratum] (default: last training year).

...

Passed to methods.

Value

An mt_draws object.

References

Brouhns N, Denuit M, Vermunt JK (2002). A Poisson log-bilinear regression approach to the construction of projected lifetables. Insurance: Mathematics and Economics 31(3): 373-393. doi:10.1016/S0167-6687(02)00185-3

Examples

x <- mt_example(deaths = "single")
fc <- mt_forecast(mt_fit(rwd(), x), h = 5, n_draws = 100, seed = 1)
fc
#> <mt_draws> Random walk with drift; origin 2019; 71 ages x 5 periods (2020-2024) x 2 strata x 100 draws
